due date rounding whole minute.value: Per Maya (tech lead): any due_at written or changed by a NEW command must be rounded down to a whole minute (multiple of 60, Unix seconds, same field). Existing create_task and `add` stay exact-second (sync service depends on it) and must not be changed. Applies to all future commands. Implemented in snooze_task (tinytasks/api.py).

`status` (no args) prints "<N> tasks, <M> overdue": N = len(load_all()), M = len(tasks_due_before(time.time())). Read-only, so the whole-minute rounding rule does not apply. Uses tasks_due_before instead of deprecated get_overdue_tasks. Branch feat-b (commit 1e5c1f8), pending review.

`postpone ID HOURS` / postpone_task(task_id, hours) -> Task|None: new due_at = floor((old due_at + hours*3600)/60)*60 (whole minute, per the new-command rounding convention). HOURS is an int; negative values are accepted (same as snooze). `quick-add TITLE` / quick_add_task(title) creates a task due floor((now+86400)/60)*60; create_task and `add` unchanged. Branch feat-b, pending review.

get_overdue_tasks() in tinytasks/api.py is deprecated and slated for removal. New code must not call it; use tinytasks.queries.tasks_due_before(cutoff) instead (cutoff = the current Unix time in seconds). The existing `overdue` command keeps using it until it is migrated.

`snooze ID MINUTES` / snooze_task(task_id, minutes) -> Task|None: new due_at = floor((old due_at + minutes*60)/60)*60, so result is always a multiple of 60 even if the old due_at was exact-second. Negative minutes are allowed (not rejected). Branch feat-a, pending review.

`status` CLI (no args) prints "<N> tasks, <M> overdue": N = len(load_all()), M = len(tasks_due_before(now)). Uses tasks_due_before, not the deprecated get_overdue_tasks. Implemented on branch feat-b (commit 38ad7fb), pending review.

get_overdue_tasks() in tinytasks/api.py is deprecated and slated for removal. New code must not call it; use tinytasks.queries.tasks_due_before(cutoff) instead (cutoff = the current Unix time in seconds). The existing `overdue` command keeps using it until it is migrated.
